name: What is the difference between a built-in and a freestanding window seat?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a built-in and a freestanding window seat?

acceptedAnswer.text: A built-in window seat is custom-made and permanently affixed to the wall or window frame, becoming an integral part of the room's architecture. It offers a seamless, tailored look and often includes custom storage solutions. A freestanding window seat, however, is a movable piece of furniture that is not attached to the structure. While it offers flexibility in arrangement, it may not perfectly fit the window area and often lacks custom features. The choice depends on whether you prefer a permanent, integrated design or a more flexible, portable option. Many homeowners in Star choose built-in options to enhance property value and create a cohesive design.
acceptedAnswer.description: Built-in window seats are permanent and custom-fitted for a seamless look, while freestanding ones are movable furniture pieces.
